requirements.label: greek-language
requirements.title: Greek language courses

rule.manualCheck: Confirm whether the student has competency in Modern Greek. If not, the student must complete the intermediate-level Modern Greek courses (GRK 211 and GRK 212).
rule.text: Greek Language Courses offered: GRK 121 (Elementary Modern Greek I, 3 credits); GRK 122 (Elementary Modern Greek II, 3 credits); GRK 211 (Intermediate Modern Greek I, 3 credits); GRK 212 (Intermediate Modern Greek II, 3 credits); GRK 321 (Advanced Modern Greek I, 3 credits); GRK 322 (Advanced Modern Greek II, 3 credits). If students do not have competency in Modern Greek language, they are required to successfully complete the Modern Greek language courses at the Intermediate level.
rule.reason: The page lists the language courses as offered but does not state a required set. The intermediate-level requirement applies only to students without competency, which cannot be checked from a transcript.

requirements.sourceText: The Greek Language Courses offered are: GRK 121 - Elementary Modern Greek I 3 credits; GRK 122 - Elementary Modern Greek II 3 credits; GRK 211 - Intermediate Modern Greek I 3 credits; GRK 212 - Intermediate Modern Greek II 3 credits; GRK 321 - Advanced Modern Greek I 3 credits; GRK 322 - Advanced Modern Greek II 3 credits. If students do not have competency in Modern Greek language, they are required to successfully complete the Modern Greek language courses at the Intermediate level.

rule.manualCheck: Verify that each course counted from another discipline is relevant to Ancient Greece, Hellenic literature, history, or culture.
rule.text: Courses in other disciplines relevant to Ancient Greece, Hellenic literature, history and culture can be used to fulfill the minor requirements.
rule.reason: The page does not list the eligible courses, and relevance is a judgment, so the pool cannot be defined as a selector.

requirements.sourceText: Courses in other disciplines relevant to Ancient Greece, Hellenic literature, history and culture can be used to fulfill the minor requirements.

policies.sourceText: Courses offered for the minor must be taken for a letter grade.
All courses offered for the minor must be passed with a grade of C or higher.
At least nine of the 21 credits must be taken at Stony Brook, with three of the courses at the upper-division level.

notes.text: Students wishing to pursue a minor in Hellenic Studies must develop a specific plan for its completion in consultation with the advisor. Director of the Minor: Dr. Stella Tsirka, styliani-anna.tsirka@stonybrook.edu, (631) 444-3859, 1052 Humanities Building.

An example of an acceptable distribution: two 100-level courses; two 200-level courses; three 300-level courses, with the option of substituting one 400-level course for one of the three 300-level courses.
Students are strongly encouraged to participate in the Summer study abroad program in Greece.
